events.summary: Described by the legendary Lydia Lunch as “harsh, hard...catchy, weird, arty" and "a very unique blend that defies category,” Portland's Nasalrod is a collaborative vision. The intensity of drummer Spit Stix \(a founding member of the seminal L.A. punk band FEAR\) is a major driving force behind the ferocious spazz-rock and roll quartet. The band is currently performing its frenetic act in support of their split 12" record with Bay Area luminaries Victims Family. This record, entitled In the Modern Meatspace, is currently available in the Alternative Tentacles catalog. The recent video for their song "The Maker" features appearances from various punk and metal legends, such as Jello Biafra \(Dead Kennedys\), Al Jourgensen \(Ministry\), and many more. Armed with a notoriously frantic live show, Nasalrod has found that originality and insanity can go hand in hand. Lead singer Chairman’s sneering, kooky yet soulful vocals soar over a sound that is simultaneously melodic, violent and convulsive. Spit Stix, guitarist Mustin Douch, and bassist Mandy Morgan provide a sonic backdrop that is the demented and freakish heart of the band. Their music has been described by weekinpop.com as “raucous and radically defiant…a party crashing cavalcade of confidence and cavalier fancy". Nasalrod has shared stages with acts such as The Jesus Lizard, Mudhoney, Melt-Banana, Mike Watt, and Big Business. “A whirlwind of punk intensity, jagged rhythms, and theatrical vocal acrobatics—exactly the kind of unhinged energy you’d expect from a band that thrives on the unpredictable.” – Tim Mudd, Decibel Magazine
events.title: Nasalrod & Gaytheist & Creature Party

events.summary: Raised in Atlanta and shaped by her Spanish heritage, Zen Selekta creates music where global rhythms collide with cinematic textures and heavyweight low end. Bridging worlds, her sound blends organic percussion with modern electronic production to create something that feels both ancient and futuristic. Known for her magnetic stage presence, Zen's performances are equal parts catharsis and celebration. On stage, she surrenders fully to the music, allowing it to move through her. She approaches every performance as a journey, building moments of tension, release, and discovery that draw listeners deeper into the experience. For Zen Selekta, music is ritual, and the dancefloor is a space for reconnecting with ourselves, each other, and the present moment.

We reserve the right to cancel any or all orders and tickets if you exceed the posted limits, including orders associated with the same name, e-mail address, billing address, credit card number or other information. w/ Gaytheist & Creature Party Alternative Tentacles Records is proud to partner with Nadine Records to present Nasalrod and their new release The "Friends" 45, a two-song 7" that takes a demented, sometimes humorous look at friendship, exploring not only what friends are for but also what might be lurking behind a friendly face. Hailing from Portland, OR and once described by legendary underground artist Lydia Lunch as “harsh, hard...catchy, weird, arty” and “a very unique blend that defies category,” Nasalrod is a collaborative vision of punk rock chaos. In their years together, Nasalrod has built a reputation for its notoriously frantic live performances and an unapologetically unhinged approach. Their music has been described by Week in Pop as “raucous and radically defianta party crashing cavalcade of confidence and cavalier fancy.” Led by Chairman's sneering, kooky yet soulful vocals, expanded by Mustin Douch’s wiley, dexterous guitar explosions, anchored by Mandy Morgan’s punchy, authoritative bass work, and driven by the relentless intensity of founding FEAR drummer Spit Stix, the quartet combines ferocious spazz-punk, warped melodies and convulsive rock and roll into a sound that is as unpredictable as it is infectious. "Friends" features a version of FEAR's “What Are Friends For?”, originally written by Spit Stix! The reworked rendition here finally brings Spit's intended vision to life. Paired with the melodic intensity of “Behind Friendly Faces”, the two tracks offer contrasting perspectives on friendship, delivered with Nasalrod's signature blend of theatrical energy, twisted humor, precise musicianship, and explosive intensity. It’s this very unhinged creative vision which has been on Jello Biafra’s radar since the release of their split with Victim’s Family, In The Modern Meatspace on Nadine Records in 2024. He’s not the only one who has noticed, as Nasalrod has been making a name for itself and has shared stages with acts such as The Jesus Lizard, Mudhoney, Melt-Banana, Mike Watt, Alice Donut, Iggy Pop and more. Recorded at Portland's Jackpot! Studios by Larry Crane (Tape Op Magazine, Sleater-Kinney, Cat Power, Elliott Smith) and mixed and mastered by Stephan Hawkes (Red Fang, High on Fire, Gaytheist), The "Friends" 45 perfectly captures Nasalrod's uniquely chaotic approach, pushing the boundaries of its own peculiar brand of punk rock and proving that originality and insanity can go hand in hand. As Joyzine.org recently stated, "In a musical climate often content with the familiar, Nasalrod’s audacity feels not only welcome but necessary." The 7" is available for wide release on black vinyl and in a limited artist edition on red vinyl available at Nasalrod shows and on the Alternative Tentacles Patreon. **NASALROD "FRIENDS" WILL RELEASE ON FRIDAY, NOVEMBER 13TH** ALL SALES ARE FINAL. The Kiki House of Jeremy Scott drops in for a vogue purrr-formance with ALoSo on decks. Opening the night is Repeat Behavior producer and resident DJ kraftwitch, and shutting it down is Troubled Youth (Judy On Duty) b2b Stas Thee Boss. Host: Angel Darko Door: Father Fannie This event is for the dolls, sapphics, theys, gays and the bitches who love us. Come one, come all for a stunty ass Fall. This will sell out, so don't sit on those tix. Kevin Aviance is a pioneering nightlife icon, recording artist, DJ, and performance legend whose influence has shaped generations of LGBTQ nightlife, dance music, and drag performance. Emerging from New York City’s underground club scene in the late 1980s as a member of the legendary House of Aviance, Kevin built a singular career that blends high-fashion spectacle, fierce choreography, and unapologetic queer expression. Known for electrifying club anthems like “Din Da Da,” “Cunty,” and “Give It Up,” Kevin became a defining voice of the early-2000s club era and an originator of the visual and performance language that helped shape modern queer nightlife. Over the course of his recording career, he released three full-length studio albums — Box of Chocolates, Entity, and HIPPOPOTAMUS! — while earning three Billboard No. 1 Dance Club singles with “Din Da Da,” “Alive,” and “Give It Up.” Those songs, along with “Rhythm Is My Bitch” and “Join In The Chant,” give Kevin five Billboard Dance Club Top 10 singles. Alongside his music career, Kevin became a sought-after DJ and live performer, bringing ballroom attitude, avant-garde drag, and high-energy performance to dance floors around the world. Kevin’s story is also one of resilience. After surviving a brutal hate crime in 2006 that shocked the LGBTQ community, Kevin became a powerful symbol of perseverance and healing. In recent years, a new generation has rediscovered his music and legacy, including a major cultural resurgence when Beyoncé sampled Kevin’s work on her album Renaissance, introducing his sound and influence to millions of new listeners. Today, Kevin continues to perform internationally while reflecting on his legacy as one of the architects of queer club culture. Through music, storytelling, and performance, he remains a living bridge between the history of underground queer nightlife and the artists shaping its future.
events.title: Repeat Behavior: Kevin Aviance (DJ Set)

events.summary: Join the Friends of Errol Heights, Portland Parks & Recreation, and Johnson Creek Watershed Council as we gather at Errol Heights Park for a morning of Land Tending! Revegetation, selective plant removal, and trash pick-up encourages plant and species diversity and builds habitats for a healthy watershed. THIS EVENT IS CANCELLED When: Saturday, December 19th, 9:00 am-12:00 pm Where: Errol Heights City Park \(directions emailed after registration\) What: Native plantings, litter pickup, and invasive weed removal. Tasks may shift as needs change at the site. How to prepare: This event will happen rain or shine, so dress for the weather! Wear long thick pants, a long-sleeved shirt, and sturdy shoes you don’t mind getting muddy. Bring a raincoat or a hat and sunscreen, as appropriate. Bring a filled water bottle and snacks! You’re welcome to bring gloves and tools, if you want to use your own. What we provide: Gloves and all necessary tools, and instruction on how to safely use tools and remove invasive weeds. We can also provide bus fare to and from the event. Please contact info@jcwc.org to arrange bus fare. Health and Safety: We will follow current Oregon Health Authority guidelines. events.summary: As the year draws toward its quietest turning point, we are invited to slow down, reconnect with the natural world, and make space for rest, reflection, and renewal. Join us for a gentle, guided forest bathing walk among the beautiful evergreen trees of Hoyt Arboretum. Inspired by the winter solstice, this two-hour experience will offer an opportunity to step away from the busyness of everyday life and immerse ourselves in the sights, sounds, scents, and quiet wisdom of the winter forest. Through mindful wandering, sensory invitations, moments of stillness, and gentle reflection, we’ll explore what it means to honor the season we’re in, release what we’re ready to set down, and welcome the possibilities of the returning light. Together, we’ll make space for: Rest: Embracing the stillness and slower rhythms of winter. Rooting: Finding grounding and connection among the trees. Release: Reflecting on the year behind us and what we’re ready to let go. Renewal: Setting gentle intentions for the season ahead. This is not a hike to conquer or a destination to reach. It’s an invitation to slow down, listen deeply, and simply be present with the living world around us. No prior forest bathing experience is needed. Come as you are, dress for the weather, and give yourself the gift of two hours in the forest. Our intention: To leave feeling a little more grounded, a little more spacious, and more connected to ourselves, one another, and the natural world. Rest. Root. Renew. Space is limited; please register online Registration closes Friday, December 18th at 4:00pm Class details will be emailed closer to the program date About the Instructor: Shawna Hartung (she/her) is a certified Forest Therapy Guide through the Association of Nature and Forest Therapy with over 20 years of experience in environmental education, leading nature-based experiences for people of all ages. With a background in social work and a deep understanding of trauma-informed care, Shawna brings a gentle, compassionate presence to her walks—honoring each person’s unique journey and creating a space of psychological and emotional safety. Her own personal experience with breast cancer has deepened her connection to the natural world and renewed her commitment to healing-centered spaces. Shawna offers walks not only as an invitation to slow down and reconnect with nature, but also as a pathway for restoration, grief-tending, and resilience—guided by the belief that nature meets us exactly where we are.
events.title: A Winter Solstice Forest Bathing Walk

Drawing on the visual techniques of sumi-e ink painting, the five sets of photographs express seasonality through portraiture, gesture, everyday objects, and atmosphere. At the same time, the artists are exploring the relationship between tradition and cultural identity as Japanese and multi-heritage Japanese artists living in Oregon, superimposing one of the most prevalent motifs in Japanese art onto a new context. The individual artists’ works will also be on display, as well as artwork from the museum’s collection.

events.summary: Lookout Landscape is an immersive art exhibition by Oregon-based artist and designer David Buckley Borden and a team of collaborators working across forestry, design, and engineering. Inspired by fire lookout towers, trail culture, and backcountry gear, the exhibition invites visitors onto a fabricated “Lookout Trail,” where a series of imaginative scenes—from a trailhead to a weather station, campground, and tool shed—reimagine the visual language of forestry and outdoor culture in the Pacific Northwest. Blending research, humor, and design, the exhibition explores the complex relationships between people and working forests, with wildfire as an underlying thread. As visitors move through the space, they are encouraged to reflect on how forests are shaped, valued, and cared for, and to consider their own connection to these landscapes. events.summary: Curated by Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK School and Lisa Jarrett Drawing from the Museum’s collection, this exhibition is co-curated by Lisa Jarrett, an artist, educator, and curator, and the Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK Elementary— a group of 4th and 5th grade curators from KSMoCA. Working from a conversation with notable curators Dr. Lowery Stokes Sims and Dr. Leslie King Hammond, the exhibition engages PAM’s collection in new dialogues shaped by emerging curatorial voices and multigenerational knowledge. From theme and concept development, through work selection, and installation, this community curators project highlights the collaborative nature of curatorial practice and museum work. Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK School \(HTC\) is a KSMoCA project. Students participate directly in shaping exhibitions, positioning them as contributors to the museum, and engaging them as researchers, writers, planners, and curators. Through workshops and field trips, students collaborate with artists, visiting curators, and mentors from Portland State University’s College of the Arts. They research how exhibitions are developed, how artworks are interpreted, and how institutional decisions shape public understanding. Expanded curatorial practice includes visual art, writing, performance, research, publishing, and social practice. Co-founded by Lisa Jarrett and Harrell Fletcher, the project began in 2018 at Harriet Tubman Middle School and continues in its current iteration at Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Elementary School.
events.title: Harriet Tubman Center Museum

events.summary: Inspired by Katherine Ace’s 9 Portraits as the foundational starting point for the exhibition, Nine Women Artists will feature the work of the artists shown in Ace’s portrait painting. All mature artists in their careers and with a significant presence in the Northwest, their work reveals a diverse expression of artistic styles from representation to abstraction. There are rich details in the painting. Most notably on the left hangs Henri Fantin-Latour’s A Studio at Les Batignolles, 1870 \(Musée d’Orsay\). In this painting is a formal gathering of male artists. In response to this painting, Katherine asked her subjects to dress in their studio/work clothes as counterpoint, all marked in their characteristic poses. Other Portland women artists are recognized here through their paintings—a small Sally Haley still life hangs in the background, as well as an Amanda Snyder painting behind Phyllis Yes. And to the far right, we have a glimpse of Lucinda Parker’s very large work. Postcards and newspapers scattered on the floor are the exhibition announcements and reviews highlighting the artists’ works. An epic portrait featuring nine women artists of the Northwest, Ace responded to the lack of self-portraits by women artists in history. From left, the artists are: Laura Ross-Paul, Katherine’s self-portrait seated with phone, Mary Josephson, Judy Cooke, Phyllis Yes, Sharon Bronzan, Shu-Ju Wang, Lucinda Parker, and Sherrie Wolf. All are women artists who have made long careers in Portland. As Ace notes about these women, “They have tenacity, have lived through sexist decades, told they couldn’t really be artists—only fit for sleeping with the professor, expected to subvert themselves to male artist machismo.”
events.title: Nine Women Artists

events.summary: Make a holiday trip to Vancouver, Washington, and experience Columbia Dance’s original Fort Vancouver Nutcracker, December 18–20 at Skyview Concert Hall. This is not your typical Nutcracker. Set in 1840s Fort Vancouver, the production weaves Tchaikovsky’s beloved score into the real history of the Pacific Northwest, with scenes inspired by the people, places, and stories of the region. Beavers, fur trappers, covered-wagon travelers, dancing wapato plants, and a mystical moon all find their way into this imaginative take on the holiday classic. Created through historical research and collaboration with local historians and Fort Vancouver National Historic Site, the production offers a distinctly Pacific Northwest interpretation of a familiar holiday tradition. Since its debut in 2021, more than 28,000 people have experienced the Fort Vancouver Nutcracker, with approximately 5,000 audience members attending each year. More than 100 student dancers and guest artists bring the production to life, presented by Columbia Dance, a nonprofit arts organization founded in 1989. Come for the ballet and make a weekend of it. Explore Fort Vancouver, the Vancouver Waterfront, local restaurants, and other holiday activities while you’re in town.
events.title: A One-of-a-Kind Nutcracker Rooted in 1840s Fort Vancouver

Son of the White Mare (1981) x Perfume for the Eyes — Between Worlds: A Multisensory Solstice Experience Enter the psychedelic, mythic world of Son of the White Mare (1981), Hungarian animator Marcell Jankovics’s extraordinary animated tale of heroic journeys, transformation, and the cyclical dance between light and darkness. As the winter solstice approaches, join visual perfumer and divinatory artist Danielle Delceppo for an immersive journey into the film’s mythological world through scent, tactile exploration, and a collective tarot reading. This multisensory experience invites audiences to engage with the film’s archetypal imagery and symbolism, finding echoes of their own stories within the myth and carrying its wisdom beyond the screen. About Danielle Delceppo Danielle Delceppo is a visual perfumer, divinatory artist, tarot reader, and astrologer whose work explores the intersection of sensory memory, symbolism, and personal narrative. She is the creator of Perfume for the Eyes: A Tarot of Dreams, a multisensory tarot deck and guidebook developed through her practice of Visual Perfumery, which translates the architecture of scent into layered imagery. Through her studio, Auburn Intuitive, she brings art, tarot, and astrology together to facilitate experiences that connect personal storytelling with shared discovery. She is the resident astrologer and tarot reader at Soho House Portland and Frances May. In 2026, she spoke on the Tarot Ecosystems panel at the Philosophical Research Society’s Festival of Tarot. events.summary: Northwest Vocal Arts (NWVA), presents its annual Voices of Winter holiday concerts on Saturday, December 19 at 3:00 p.m. and Sunday, December 20 at 7:00 pm p.m. at Rose City Park United Methodist Church, located at 5830 NE Alameda St. in Portland. The theme of this year’s concerts is Peace on Earth and will highlight music with a message of peace and the unifying spirit of forgiveness and hope. The winter concert will feature the NWVA Olympia professional chamber choir, featuring some of the finest vocalists in our area, joined by the NWVA Evergreen youth choir. The program will include Peace on Earth by the American composer Amy Beach, Dona Nobis Pacem from Haydn’s Missa in Angustiis (Mass for Troubled Times) as well as Iesous ahatonnia by Canadian composer Sarah Quartel, which invites the audience to reflect on the truths of the past while preparing for a brighter future. Samuel Barbara, Executive and Artistic Director of NWVA says of these concerts, “the holidays offer us a time to slow down and reflect on what we are grateful for and music helps us process our emotions. This past year has been one of particular divisiveness and geopolitical tension, and we felt a concert promoting peace would be particularly appropriate.”

events.summary: Your monthly ritual... An invitation to come back to center. Our nervous systems are constantly taking in information. Between work, screens, notifications, responsibilities, and the general pace of everyday life, our attention is often being pulled in multiple directions at once—with very little intentional time to slow down and rest. This monthly nervous system reset is a dedicated space to do exactly that: support nervous system regulation. This immersive sound bath experience uses crystal singing bowls, chimes, oceanic textures, and other therapeutic sounds to gently guide your system out of the noise and stimulation of everyday life and into a deeper state of rest. For 75-minutes, there’s nowhere else you need to be and nothing you need to do. Simply get comfortable, receive the sound, and allow yourself to unwind. Think of this as your recurring monthly ritual to come back to center - a space to intentionally step away from the busyness of life, reconnect with yourself, and give your body and mind the restoration you're craving. Come as you are. Yoga mats, blankets, and props are available for your use, but please feel free to bring anything that will help you feel even more cozy & comfortable. These sessions are open to all; no prior experience is needed. About Kristi Kristi Littman is a certified sound healing practitioner & facilitation teacher whose heart-led approach blends nervous system awareness, intuition, and deep presence. Since 2019, Kristi has held space for thousands of people through community sound baths, corporate wellness, sound healing training, and 1:1 mentorship. She blends crystal singing bowls, chimes, and oceanic tones to create immersive soundscapes designed to soothe the nervous system and realign the body’s natural rhythms. She often weaves in meditation and breathwork, offering grounded, intuitive guidance that helps participants soften, release, and remember their own inner wisdom. Benefits of Sound Therapy: Deep relaxation & stress relief Release tension Energy cleansing & balancing Improved mental focus Enhanced meditation & mindfulness Emotional release Physical healing support Spiritual connection Improved sleep Enhanced creativity & problem-solving Moments of clarity Deep rest
events.title: RITUAL: Immersive Soundbath

events.summary: Harmonic Movement Contemporary Dance is a practice that invites each dancer to discover and infuse their own movement story and embodied voice into every movement and phrase. Drawing on the vocabularies of ballet, jazz, and modern dance, each class offers dancers of any age or experience level a way in that fits their own body, movement history, and expressive tendencies. A thorough warm-up helps dancers access their optimal strength and mobility, building both freedom and control before moving into playful and creative technique-building exercises and center choreography. At its heart, Harmonic Movement Contemporary Dance is about joy: the joy of movement, of dancing together, and discovering the ways creative expression can be genuinely healing.

events.summary: Gina DeNoble is a vocalist and songwriter currently living in the Portland, Oregon area. She plays guitar and delivers deep, textured, resonant, sultry vocals. Her genre is lyric-driven, soulful folk with occasional blues elements. The mood of her music could be described as dramatic, whimsical, emotional, and romantic. Artists to whom she has been compared include Tracy Chapman, Natalie Merchant, and Joan Armatrading. Having grown up a stone’s throw from Mount Rainier National Park, Gina is a dyed-in-the-wool Pacific Northwesterner! Her debut full-length album entitled Wanderer’s Paradise is currently streaming on all major platforms. The songs on the album were written while she was traveling regularly between Washington, Canada, and Alaska. Gina returned to the stage in 2023 after an almost 15-year hiatus from giving public performances. She has since been playing at venues and festivals around the Pacific Northwest region. She made her debut at Seattle’s Northwest Folklife Festival, returned to the beloved mountain lodge where she lived as a teen and wrote several of the songs on her album, played an off-grid outdoor hydroelectric-powered concert at Breitenbush Hot Springs, helped kick off the Washougal Songcraft Festival, and was a featured guest on the national radio program River City Folk with Tom May.
events.title: Local Roots Music Inspiring Artists Songwriter Series

events.summary: Make a holiday trip to Vancouver, Washington, and experience Columbia Dance’s original Fort Vancouver Nutcracker, December 18–20 at Skyview Concert Hall. This is not your typical Nutcracker. Set in 1840s Fort Vancouver, the production weaves Tchaikovsky’s beloved score into the real history of the Pacific Northwest, with scenes inspired by the people, places, and stories of the region. Beavers, fur trappers, covered-wagon travelers, dancing wapato plants, and a mystical moon all find their way into this imaginative take on the holiday classic. Created through historical research and collaboration with local historians and Fort Vancouver National Historic Site, the production offers a distinctly Pacific Northwest interpretation of a familiar holiday tradition. Since its debut in 2021, more than 28,000 people have experienced the Fort Vancouver Nutcracker, with approximately 5,000 audience members attending each year. More than 100 student dancers and guest artists bring the production to life, presented by Columbia Dance, a nonprofit arts organization founded in 1989. Come for the ballet and make a weekend of it. Explore Fort Vancouver, the Vancouver Waterfront, local restaurants, and other holiday activities while you’re in town.
events.title: A One-of-a-Kind Nutcracker Rooted in 1840s Fort Vancouver

events.summary: God is a Frog Heaven is a Swamp is the second studio album by Los Angeles-based band Dark Dazey. Self-ascribed as ‘frog rock,’ the sonics hop between hazy, atmospheric ‘swampscapes’ and country-fried garage rock, stitched together into a vivid, genre-blending collage. Set against the backdrop of late-stage capitalism and low-grade existential dread, Dark Dazey trades cynicism for something equal parts strange and playful: swampy escapism rooted in the belief that there really is something beautiful out there in the muck. They recast the swamp as a place of joy, humor, and possibility. A place to be worshipped, never drained. Blending the offbeat experimental spirit of Ween, the laid-back surrealism of Mac DeMarco, and the playful satire of Viagra Boys, God is a Frog Heaven is a Swamp sounds a bit like the Grateful Dead dosed Jimmy Buffett. It’s an album best experienced with your feet in the water and a cold drink in hand… or atop a lily pad.

events.summary: At the height of the holiday season, a group of workers and their families discover that their wages are going to be cut. Together, they decide to fight for a better life. As the struggle drags on, they find joy and community through the music and stories of their different traditions….and of this new world they now share. Featuring early 20th century American classics, alongside songs and folktales from Eastern Europe, Italy, the Philippines, and the Latin American diaspora, Bread and Roses celebrates the tapestry of people who helped to build this country, proclaiming "We all deserve joy, We all deserve beauty!" Portland Revels' annual holiday Midwinter Revels production celebrates the winter solstice and the return of the light at the darkest time of year. Each season the production is set in a different place and time, allowing us to explore different cultures and music traditions, while grounding the show in our familiar rituals and themes.
events.title: Portland Revels presents "Bread and Roses"

When Oralene, the guiding force behind the production suddenly passes away, the tight-knit group of women she left behind—known as the Silver Belles—must step up to save the show. As they fumble through rehearsals and face old wounds, they rediscover their voices, their strength, and their deep bond with one another. With twangy new country tunes, holiday classics, and plenty of Southern charm, "The Silver Belles" rings in the season with community and the kind of chosen family that helps us find our place—even when we feel a little lost. events.summary: You can’t know Beats Antique until you’ve been a part of its journey, and experienced the act as an entity with a life of its own. A stage show that demands more music; music that needs costumes, ships and masks and shadow dances; an audience that comes for art, and takes away stories to feed their imagination. When Beats Antique first drew breath, there was no pressure to become anything. The first album was just Zoe, David, and Tommy’s one-off experimental project for entertainment executive Miles Copeland, when Zoe performed with his Bellydance Superstars. From that creative freedom, a family formed, and in a good family each member wears many hats. Tommy steering percussion, piano, and music production. Zoe producing music, choosing themes and commanding a circus of travelling set designs, creating costuming, and, of course, dancing like nothing you’ve ever seen. David as the multi-instrumentalist, captain of banjo, songwriting, and production. These diverse skills are the muscle of the monster, how the creature moves through them, making itself real. Some music evolved organically from the decades of experience each collaborator brings to the project. Other pieces were written for the show. In deeply vulnerable interplay, every song is woven into a tapestry of danced and drummed story. Commitment to the full performance art form is how Beats Antique fuses musical worlds, pulling on global sounds for experiments on the fringes of cinematic cabaret, informed by electronic mash-ups and inspirations who have joined them on the journey such as Les Claypool, Bassnectar, Alam Khan, The Glitch Mob, and the Preservation Hall Jazz Band. Each album and stage show has built upon the last, with highlights such as: emergence from the bellydance and bass underground in the San Francisco Bay; performing to a massive crowd at Red Rocks Amphitheater; Thievery Corporation and their management discovering Beats Antique one fateful night at Burning Man; artist friends painting set pieces, or donning masks for the finale; performing in Egypt on the day some said the world would end; and playing a hometown show at The Fox on the night Occupy Oakland was evicted and merged with their fans to light bonfires in the street and leap over the flames. Beats Antique is lifted in each step by loyal fans who are included in their definition of chosen family. Whether they’ve been music producers or appreciators, acrobats, illustrators, or students of Zoe’s, the multigenerational, welcoming faces in the crowd are the fire that keeps Beats Antique warm, and ready to explore new depths for the sake of these many muses. They aim for a show anyone can enjoy, a circus that feeds the spirit. In this place, where they can teach and create and converse with their creation like it’s a dragon come to life full of riddles and blustery demands, Beats Antique is weaving a unique story. All shows at REALM are 21\+
events.title: Beats Antique

events.summary: Lookout Landscape is an immersive art exhibition by Oregon-based artist and designer David Buckley Borden and a team of collaborators working across forestry, design, and engineering. Inspired by fire lookout towers, trail culture, and backcountry gear, the exhibition invites visitors onto a fabricated “Lookout Trail,” where a series of imaginative scenes—from a trailhead to a weather station, campground, and tool shed—reimagine the visual language of forestry and outdoor culture in the Pacific Northwest. Blending research, humor, and design, the exhibition explores the complex relationships between people and working forests, with wildfire as an underlying thread. As visitors move through the space, they are encouraged to reflect on how forests are shaped, valued, and cared for, and to consider their own connection to these landscapes. Plan your visit and explore the exhibition: worldforestry.org/lookout-landscape

events.summary: Curated by Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK School and Lisa Jarrett Drawing from the Museum’s collection, this exhibition is co-curated by Lisa Jarrett, an artist, educator, and curator, and the Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK Elementary— a group of 4th and 5th grade curators from KSMoCA. Working from a conversation with notable curators Dr. Lowery Stokes Sims and Dr. Leslie King Hammond, the exhibition engages PAM’s collection in new dialogues shaped by emerging curatorial voices and multigenerational knowledge. From theme and concept development, through work selection, and installation, this community curators project highlights the collaborative nature of curatorial practice and museum work. Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK School \(HTC\) is a KSMoCA project. Students participate directly in shaping exhibitions, positioning them as contributors to the museum, and engaging them as researchers, writers, planners, and curators. Through workshops and field trips, students collaborate with artists, visiting curators, and mentors from Portland State University’s College of the Arts. They research how exhibitions are developed, how artworks are interpreted, and how institutional decisions shape public understanding. Expanded curatorial practice includes visual art, writing, performance, research, publishing, and social practice. Co-founded by Lisa Jarrett and Harrell Fletcher, the project began in 2018 at Harriet Tubman Middle School and continues in its current iteration at Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Elementary School.
events.title: Harriet Tubman Center Museum

events.summary: Inspired by Katherine Ace’s 9 Portraits as the foundational starting point for the exhibition, Nine Women Artists will feature the work of the artists shown in Ace’s portrait painting. All mature artists in their careers and with a significant presence in the Northwest, their work reveals a diverse expression of artistic styles from representation to abstraction. There are rich details in the painting. Most notably on the left hangs Henri Fantin-Latour’s A Studio at Les Batignolles, 1870 \(Musée d’Orsay\). In this painting is a formal gathering of male artists. In response to this painting, Katherine asked her subjects to dress in their studio/work clothes as counterpoint, all marked in their characteristic poses. Other Portland women artists are recognized here through their paintings—a small Sally Haley still life hangs in the background, as well as an Amanda Snyder painting behind Phyllis Yes. And to the far right, we have a glimpse of Lucinda Parker’s very large work. Postcards and newspapers scattered on the floor are the exhibition announcements and reviews highlighting the artists’ works. An epic portrait featuring nine women artists of the Northwest, Ace responded to the lack of self-portraits by women artists in history. From left, the artists are: Laura Ross-Paul, Katherine’s self-portrait seated with phone, Mary Josephson, Judy Cooke, Phyllis Yes, Sharon Bronzan, Shu-Ju Wang, Lucinda Parker, and Sherrie Wolf. All are women artists who have made long careers in Portland. As Ace notes about these women, “They have tenacity, have lived through sexist decades, told they couldn’t really be artists—only fit for sleeping with the professor, expected to subvert themselves to male artist machismo.”
events.title: Nine Women Artists

events.summary: The Bylines are a Portland based band created by Reece Marshburn and Marianna Thielen who write and perform sophisticated, jazz-inspired, story-driven pop music. They tour the Northwest regularly as a duo, and put on theatrical shows with their full ensemble. They are alumni of the Johnny Mercer Songwriters Project and have played before Randy Newman. Portland's The Bylines exists in a unique musical plane, one at once grounded in the big-band past of glamorous pop performances and rooted in a present realm of intricate and highly addictive songwriting. With a focus on grand live spectacle--a facet of music often lost in the digital age--the group is equally at home in velvet-curtained jazz halls, large rooms and intimate venues. That sound is the product of a marriage both sonic and literal. The Bylines is made up of two songwriters whose styles and influences converge to bring The Bylines' catchy, addictive sounds to vibrant life. Frontwoman Marianna Thielen, the glamorous face of the group, brings to the fore a background in composition, classical vocal work and, most obviously, musical theater, illuminating the stage with endlessly watchable bravado backed up by her powerful -- yet playful -- vocal prowess. Meanwhile, gliding his fingers across the keys is Reece Marshburn, letting loose a symphony of intricate melodies rooted in a combination of classical, jazz and pop music. The resulting combination is a unique pop confection drawing on decades of influences, as if Cole Porter, Carole King, Dusty Springfield, Freddie Mercury, Paul Simon, Rufus Wainwright and Regina Spektor combined forces and filtered their unique compositions through classical maestros and film composers, then sprinkled it with a keen pop sensibility and a commitment to putting on the most involving, charismatic and personalized live shows this side of the Copacabana. The Bylines have used their unique-yet-familiar sound to play to audiences large and small throughout the country, and have released both a studio\(self titled, recorded by Bob Stark at Kung Fu Bakery\) and a live album\(The Bylines Live, recorded at the Alberta Rose Theatre in Portland, OR\). The Bylines are proud alumni of the Johnny Mercer Songwriting Project, and have had support from the Regional Arts and Culture Council. Whether performing as a Thielen/Marshburn duo or with a larger band, the result is a blend of butter-smooth melodies, densely layered songwriting and powerful vocals. Most importantly, though, The Bylines musical cocktail goes down easy, and emphasizes something that is so often forgotten when such prolific songwriters present their craft: listening to music is, above all, supposed to be an experience… and a fun one.
events.title: The Bylines

events.summary: At the height of the holiday season, a group of workers and their families discover that their wages are going to be cut. Together, they decide to fight for a better life. As the struggle drags on, they find joy and community through the music and stories of their different traditions….and of this new world they now share. Featuring early 20th century American classics, alongside songs and folktales from Eastern Europe, Italy, the Philippines, and the Latin American diaspora, Bread and Roses celebrates the tapestry of people who helped to build this country, proclaiming "We all deserve joy, We all deserve beauty!" Portland Revels' annual holiday Midwinter Revels production celebrates the winter solstice and the return of the light at the darkest time of year. Each season the production is set in a different place and time, allowing us to explore different cultures and music traditions, while grounding the show in our familiar rituals and themes.

events.summary: Make a holiday trip to Vancouver, Washington, and experience Columbia Dance’s original Fort Vancouver Nutcracker, December 18–20 at Skyview Concert Hall. This is not your typical Nutcracker. Set in 1840s Fort Vancouver, the production weaves Tchaikovsky’s beloved score into the real history of the Pacific Northwest, with scenes inspired by the people, places, and stories of the region. Beavers, fur trappers, covered-wagon travelers, dancing wapato plants, and a mystical moon all find their way into this imaginative take on the holiday classic. Created through historical research and collaboration with local historians and Fort Vancouver National Historic Site, the production offers a distinctly Pacific Northwest interpretation of a familiar holiday tradition. Since its debut in 2021, more than 28,000 people have experienced the Fort Vancouver Nutcracker, with approximately 5,000 audience members attending each year. More than 100 student dancers and guest artists bring the production to life, presented by Columbia Dance, a nonprofit arts organization founded in 1989. Come for the ballet and make a weekend of it. Explore Fort Vancouver, the Vancouver Waterfront, local restaurants, and other holiday activities while you’re in town.
events.title: A One-of-a-Kind Nutcracker Rooted in 1840s Fort Vancouver

events.summary: Based on the popular comic strip by Harold Gray, Annie has become a worldwide phenomenon and was the winner of seven Tony Awards, including Best Musical. The beloved book and score by Tony Award winners, Thomas Meehan, Charles Strouse and Martin Charnin, features some of the greatest musical theatre hits ever written, including "Tomorrow." With equal measures of pluck and positivity, little orphan Annie charms everyone's hearts despite a next-to-nothing start in 1930s New York City. She is determined to find the parents who abandoned her years ago on the doorstep of a New York City Orphanage that is run by the cruel, embittered Miss Hannigan. With the help of the other girls in the Orphanage, Annie escapes to the wondrous world of NYC. In adventure after fun-filled adventure, Annie foils Miss Hannigan's evil machinations... and even befriends President Franklin Delano Roosevelt! She finds a new home and family in billionaire, Oliver Warbucks, his personal secretary, Grace Farrell, and a lovable mutt named Sandy.

events.summary: Sunday, December 20 @ 3:00 PM – 5:00 PM Portland premiere of a Christmas cult-classic from Japan! Directed by storied mogul and industry disruptor Haruki Kadokawa, and released two weeks before Jurassic Park, Rex: A Dinosaur’s Story emerges from amber today as an examplar of a bygone era of Japanese blockbusters. It follows Chie (Yumi Adachi), the young daughter of a palaeontologist who soon befriends an adorable T-Rex. As everyone seeks to exploit the dino-discovery for profit, the pair soon find themselves on the run from shady men in black and profiteers forcing Rex to act and model for endless advertisements and merchandise (pointing to the film’s actual promotional campaign, the “media-mix” strategy that spanned toys, a CLAMP manga and songs even cementing the popularity of Kentucky Fried Chicken as a de facto Christmas tradition in Japan). Featuring expressive creature effects by Carlo Rambaldi (Alien, E.T., Possession); chase scenes by carriage, snowmobile and hot air balloon; in-camera height jokes and tokusatsu-indebted “suit-mation”, as well as startling Christmas imagery, Rex is as adorable as it is unhinged, functioning as both wholesome holiday crowd-pleaser and cult curio in the making, available in the West and remastered in high definition for the very first time! Screened in Japanese with English subtitles.
events.title: Rex: A Dinosaur’s Story

events.summary: Sundays 4:30PM - 5:30PM, Oct 4 - Dec 20 | $10/weekly drop in Need a reset for your busy week ahead? Join us Sunday late afternoons for a welcoming, beginner-friendly yoga class focused on foundational poses, mindful movement, breath awareness, and building confidence on the mat. Whether you’re brand new to yoga or looking to reconnect with the fundamentals, this class is designed to help you build a strong foundation through accessible movement, breath work, and foundational poses. We’ll focus on alignment, balance, flexibility, and body awareness in a welcoming, supportive environment. Beginners are encouraged to join, and those with a regular practice will also benefit from slowing down, refining technique, and deepening their understanding of familiar poses. Options and modifications will be offered throughout class so everyone can move at their own pace. Wear comfortable athletic clothes, bring a yoga mat if possible \(a limited number will be available to borrow\), and please arrive 5–10 minutes before class begins so we can start on time. Classes are led by Wyle O'Neill, from Love Our Practice, whose yoga journey began in high school and later led him to study in Mysore and Goa, India, where he deepened his understanding of yoga’s roots and philosophy. Wyle completed his 200-hour RYT training at Yoga Salt with Tamal Dodge and completed his 500-hour teacher training at Sthira Yoga School in Goa, India. His teaching blends accessible movement, meditation, breathwork through an individual-centered practice to help students feel grounded, present, as well as connected to themselves and community.

events.summary: Make a holiday trip to Vancouver, Washington, and experience Columbia Dance’s original Fort Vancouver Nutcracker, December 18–20 at Skyview Concert Hall. This is not your typical Nutcracker. Set in 1840s Fort Vancouver, the production weaves Tchaikovsky’s beloved score into the real history of the Pacific Northwest, with scenes inspired by the people, places, and stories of the region. Beavers, fur trappers, covered-wagon travelers, dancing wapato plants, and a mystical moon all find their way into this imaginative take on the holiday classic. Created through historical research and collaboration with local historians and Fort Vancouver National Historic Site, the production offers a distinctly Pacific Northwest interpretation of a familiar holiday tradition. Since its debut in 2021, more than 28,000 people have experienced the Fort Vancouver Nutcracker, with approximately 5,000 audience members attending each year. More than 100 student dancers and guest artists bring the production to life, presented by Columbia Dance, a nonprofit arts organization founded in 1989. Come for the ballet and make a weekend of it. Explore Fort Vancouver, the Vancouver Waterfront, local restaurants, and other holiday activities while you’re in town.
events.title: A One-of-a-Kind Nutcracker Rooted in 1840s Fort Vancouver

events.summary: Celebrate Gothmas at Holocene on December 20, on the eve of the shortest, darkest day of the year. Bask in solstice gloom with three dark wave tributes: Constant Debauchery (Depeche Mode), Kiss Me Kiss Me Kiss Me (The Cure), and Precious Machinery (Siouxsie and the Banshees). Dress in black, move your beautiful shadow on the dance floor, and sing along to the songs that will keep this night alive. Constant Debauchery Constant Debauchery is the PNW’s premier Depeche Mode tribute, delivering the shadowy synths, brooding grooves, and dark-dance hooks that shaped generations. From club-floor favorites to stadium-sized anthems, they unleash pulse-pounding sets drawn from over 40 years of Depeche Mode’s enduring — and still evolving — legacy. Kiss Me Kiss Me Kiss Me Kiss Me Kiss Me Kiss Me is Portland’s definitive five-piece tribute to The Cure, delivering the shimmering guitars, aching melodies, and big-hair energy of Robert Smith’s best eras. From the darkest dirges to the brightest pop anthems, they play all the hits with heart, haze, and a healthy dose of melancholy. Precious Machinery Precious Machinery is Portland’s all-femme Siouxsie and the Banshees tribute — all eyeliner, all the time. Delivering razor-sharp renditions of the band’s iconic hits, they conjure the dark glamour of Siouxsie at her peak. A faithful tribute with a fierce edge, built for filling the dance floor.
events.title: Gothmas: Constant Debauchery (Depeche Mode), Kiss Me Kiss Me Kiss Me (The Cure), Precious Machinery (Siouxsie and the Banshees)

events.summary: Decades after her first fabled Nutcracker fever dream, Clara, no longer the child she once was, finds herself once again tumbling into a world of wonderment. Step into a holiday where tradition is turned upside down and inside out. ’Twas the Night Before Nutcracker is a glittering, whimsical journey through Clara’s holiday eve. What begins with a lively soirée and an innocent absinthe toast unravels into a dreamscape of marching soldiers, mischievous mice, swirling snowflakes, and sugarplum visions. Set to Can Can’s original adaptation of the iconic Nutcracker score, the show features new original songs alongside beloved holiday classics, a festive script, magical choreography, and stunning visuals. The spectacle weaves together classic, modern, aerial, and burlesque performances with Can Can’s refined cabaret style. Sprinkle in the perfect amount of comedy, and a touch of theatrical spark, and you’ve got a show as enchanting as it is unexpected. With its blend of elegance, humor, high kicks, and holiday spirit, ‘Twas the Night Before Nutcracker is a new holiday tradition in the making.
events.title: Can Can's 'Twas the Night Before Nutcracker

events.summary: Cedric Watson & Bijou Creole resurrect the ancient sounds of the French and Spanish contra dance and bourré alongside the spiritual rhythms of the Congo tribes of West Africa, who were sold as slaves in the Carribean and Louisiana by the French and Spanish. With an apparently bottomless repertoire of songs at his fingertips, Cedric plays everything from forgotten Creole melodies and obscure Dennis McGee reels to more modern Cajun and Zydeco songs, even occasionally throwing in a bluegrass fiddle tune or an old string band number. Unlike many of his contemporaries, he is also a prolific songwriter, writing almost all of his songs on his double row Hohner accordion. Cedric’s songs channel his diverse ancestry (African, French, Native American and Spanish) to create his own brand of sounds.

events.summary: Northwest Vocal Arts (NWVA), presents its annual Voices of Winter holiday concerts on Saturday, December 19 at 3:00 p.m. and Sunday, December 20 at 7:00 pm p.m. at Rose City Park United Methodist Church, located at 5830 NE Alameda St. in Portland. The theme of this year’s concerts is Peace on Earth and will highlight music with a message of peace and the unifying spirit of forgiveness and hope. The winter concert will feature the NWVA Olympia professional chamber choir, featuring some of the finest vocalists in our area, joined by the NWVA Evergreen youth choir. The program will include Peace on Earth by the American composer Amy Beach, Dona Nobis Pacem from Haydn’s Missa in Angustiis (Mass for Troubled Times) as well as Iesous ahatonnia by Canadian composer Sarah Quartel, which invites the audience to reflect on the truths of the past while preparing for a brighter future. Samuel Barbara, Executive and Artistic Director of NWVA says of these concerts, “the holidays offer us a time to slow down and reflect on what we are grateful for and music helps us process our emotions. This past year has been one of particular divisiveness and geopolitical tension, and we felt a concert promoting peace would be particularly appropriate.”
events.title: Northwest Vocal Arts Holiday Concerts Voices of Winter: Peace on Earth

Patterson Hood is an acclaimed singer-songwriter, guitarist, and co-founder of the Southern rock band Drive-By Truckers. Born in Muscle Shoals, Alabama, Hood grew up immersed in the region's rich musical heritage, with his father, David Hood, being a renowned session bassist for the Muscle Shoals Rhythm Section. Drawing inspiration from storytelling traditions and a passion for rock, country, and soul, Hood's music often explores themes of Southern identity, social justice, and personal introspection. While best known as frontman, singer, songwriter, and guitar player for Drive-By Truckers, he is also a writer of essays, columns, and short stories as well as a solo performer and producer. Since forming Drive-By Truckers in 1996 with Mike Cooley, Hood has been a driving force behind the band’s narrative-driven sound, blending gritty, guitar-heavy arrangements with evocative lyrics. Albums like Southern Rock Opera (2001) and The Dirty South (2004) have solidified their reputation as one of the most influential Southern rock bands of their generation. Beyond his work with the Truckers, Hood has released solo albums including Killers and Stars (2004) and Heat Lightning Rumbles in the Distance (2012), showcasing his versatility as a songwriter. His latest solo album, Exploding Trees & Airplane Screams, produced by Chris Funk (The Decemberists) and released via ATO Records in February 2025, earned widespread critical acclaim, including 9/10 from Uncut and 8/10 from Mojo. Pitchfork called it Hood’s “most adventurous and surprising, and his best” solo record, while Forbes praised it as “one of Hood’s most focused studio efforts.” Whether fronting the Truckers or performing solo, Hood remains a vital force in contemporary Americana and Southern rock, celebrated for turning life’s raw realities into compelling, soul-stirring art. Since their humble beginnings as high-school best friends almost two decades ago (the band formed in 2006), they have been grinding away tour after tour - visiting over 25 countries - and album after album - this is their 10th LP. Their sound has always evolved as they have grown, and worked with different labels and producers, but it has always stayed true to the psychedelic vision those kids had years ago at the very beginning. They say their new album Can’t Stop Coming Around (Tender Loving Empire Records) is their favorite, and represents their sound the best of any in their discography. It makes sense considering they recorded it themselves at their home studio ‘FFF’ in Portland, Oregon. Teaming up with Collin Hegna (Brian Jonestown Massacre, Federale - someone the band has worked with on and off since 2010), they say this is the closest they’ve ever come to hitting the bullseye in the studio. Now with Can’t Stop Coming Around slated for release this summer, the band will embark on tours of Europe (one in June and another in September), then in the USA hitting the West Coast in July and August, and the East Coast later this fall. As a group that has always tried to lead with honesty and to shake off any airs of pretense, The Shivas have come into their own. Visitors will enjoy festive displays across nineteen rooms in the Mansion and four in the Gate Lodge, each artfully decorated to reflect a nesting of five iconic decades - from the 1910s through the 1950s. And you will love the grand foyer - it's being decorated to wow you. It's that time of the year again when one can step into the magic of the season at Portland's favorite historical home, Pittock Mansion. Experience the warmth, wonder, and nostalgia of timeless holiday stories and traditions, beautifully brought to life throughout the incredible rooms of the Mansion and the charming Gate Lodge. More than seventy community volunteers and interior designers contribute their time, talent, creativity, and resources to decorate their beloved mansion. This holiday tradition has been ongoing since 1965, when the mansion was restored and reopened to the public. On select weekends, Santa will be delighting visitors and live musicians and choir performances will add to the holiday mirth. events.summary: From Warner Bros. Pictures and Legendary Pictures comes Dune: Part Three, bringing Academy Award-nominated filmmaker Denis Villeneuve’s epic trilogy to a breathtaking conclusion. Dune: Part Three is set nearly two decades after Paul Atreides seized control of the Imperium. Now a ruthless Emperor, Paul must face the consequences of his reign as old allies return, terrifying new threats emerge, and betrayal lurks in every shadow. Haunted by visions of Imperial collapse and the reappearance of his long-lost love, Paul is drawn into a sweeping conspiracy, with Chani at the heart of its unfolding mystery. As rebellion brews and enemies close in, Paul must confront the true cost of power and the fate of those he loves the most. The film stars Oscar nominee Timothée Chalamet, Zendaya, Jason Momoa, Oscar nominee Florence Pugh, Rebecca Ferguson, Isaach de Bankolé, with Oscar nominee Charlotte Rampling, with Anya Taylor-Joy, and Robert Pattinson, and Oscar winner Javier Bardem. Villeneuve directs from a screenplay by Villeneuve and Brian K. Vaughan, based on the novels written by Frank Herbert. The film is produced by Oscar nominees Mary Parent, Cale Boyter, Villeneuve and Tanya Lapointe, and Joe Caracciolo, and executive produced by Joshua Grode, Thomas Tull, Herbert W. Gains, Brian Herbert, Byron Merritt, Kim Herbert, Kevin J. Anderson, Richard P. Rubinstein, John Harrison and Jessica Derhammer. Joining Villeneuve behind the camera are Oscar-winning director of photography Linus Sandgren, Oscar-winning production designer Patrice Vermette, Oscar-winning editor Joe Walker, Oscar nominated costume designer Jacqueline West, Oscar-nominated casting director Francine Maisler, and Oscar-winning composer Hans Zimmer. Warner Bros. Pictures and Legendary Pictures Present A Legendary Pictures Production, A Film By Denis Villeneuve, Dune: Part Three, only in cinemas December 17, 2026. The film will be distributed worldwide by Warner Bros. Pictures and in China by Legendary East.

The Benson Portland, Curio Collection by Hilton, invites the community to celebrate one of Portland's most beloved holiday traditions - the 54th Annual Gingerbread Unveiling - filling the hotel's grand lobby with the warmth, wonder, and joy of the season. Guests of all ages are welcome to enjoy live music, children's activities, a hot chocolate station, a surprise visit from Santa, and more as The Benson kicks off the holidays in true Portland style. Each year, Chef Diffendorfer and his team bring to life imaginative creations that capture the spirit of the season and showcase extraordinary craftsmanship. The Benson is proud to continue its partnership with FOX 12 and Les Schwab Tire Centers' Toy Drive. Guests are encouraged to bring a new, unwrapped toy to help brighten the holidays for local children and families in need. "The Gingerbread Unveiling has been a cherished tradition at The Benson for over five decades," said Ryan Kunzer, General Manager. events.summary: Our Foundation series is designed for anyone new to the practice of improvisation and for those wishing to re-learn or deepen their practice of the art form's basics. We welcome people from all backgrounds, both creative and non-creative, so no acting or performing skills are ever required: just a desire to have fun, trust your instincts, and learn! Students should expect to learn: 👂🏼New ways of listening 🎁 The gifts of staying in the moment 📚 Telling spontaneous stories with others 👣 Thinking on our feet & trusting our instincts 👥 Quickly collaborating with others 👀 Identifying & using non-verbal communication 💪🏼 Discovering our strengths Why Take Classes With Us? Change Through Play's studio is founded on the belief that student progress only comes from providing clear instruction and feedback. We not only want our students to learn the core skills of improvisation, but we also want them to IMPROVE over their time with us. Because of that, we offer learning opportunities that students won't find anywhere else, including: A safe, nurturing, and supportive environment 10 students max per class, so each gets lots of attention Coaching and check-ins throughout each class Blackboard discussions, to help visual and analytical learners Closing every class with students recognizing their own wins Receiving highly personalized notes from your teacher, celebrating your wins during the class series & recommending skills to work on when you come back for another class with us. Sagal has traveled all around the country with Wait Wait...Don’t Tell Me! playing to sold-out theaters from Seattle to Miami. As one of the nation's premier radio humorists and commentators on current events, Peter speaks about the intersections of politics, civics, humor and entertainment, and how they all draw from each other to create the American experience. An adept moderator, Sagal is also the perfect emcee, able to apply his quick wit to esoteric company stories, weaving in jokes for an uproarious and unforgettable evening. Whether providing insightful, colorful commentary on current events or a behind-the- scenes peek at the funniest show on radio, Sagal never fails to inform and entertain. Peter Sagal is, has been, and perhaps someday will be again, a husband, father, playwright, screenwriter, author, journalist, columnist, marathoner, Jeopardy contestant, dramaturg, podcast host, documentary host, foreign correspondent, wedding officiant, and magician’s assistant. In 1997, Peter got a call from a friend telling him about a new show at NPR, which was looking for “funny people who read a lot of newspapers.” He auditioned and appeared as a panelist on the first broadcast of Wait, Wait Don’t Tell Me! in January of 1998, and moved with his family to Chicago to become the host in May, alongside our original judge and scorekeeper, Carl Kasell. In the two decades since, he has traveled the country with the show, playing in venues such as the Pritzker Pavilion at Millennium Park, Red Rocks, Tanglewood, the San Francisco War Memorial Opera House, and Carnegie Hall. He’s interviewed two Presidents, a number of Nobel Prize winners, astronauts and rocket scientists, musicians Elvis Costello, Yo Yo Ma, and Ice Cube, actors Tom Hanks and Scarlet Johansson and many, many others. Wait, Wait has grown from 50,000 weekly listeners on nine stations at its launch to over five million listeners on more than 700 stations, making it the most listened-to hour in public radio. This, however, has not gone to his head. In 2008, he accepted a Peabody award on behalf of the panelists, crew and producers of this show. He’s also won the Kurt Vonnegut Award for Humor from the Kurt Vonnegut Library. He’s the author of The Book of Vice: Naughty T and The Incomplete Book of Running, a memoir about the 2013 Boston Marathon Bombing and other adventures while running long distances. He’s contributed essays to Opera News, Saveur, Finesse, The New York Times Magazine , and was the “Road Scholar” columnist for Runner’s World. He has three daughters, Rosie, Gracie and Willa, and lives in the Chicago area with his wife Mara and two dogs, DeeDee and Dutchie, who like to see their names in print. This Event is All Ages and Reserved Seating. ALL SALES ARE FINAL. PLEASE, DOUBLE CHECK YOUR ORDER BEFORE PURCHASING. NO REFUNDS.

events.summary: Lloyd Jones is a consummate guitarist/singer/songwriter/arranger/performer/ bandleader. One of the most original artists on the modern day blues scene, Jones is, in the words of Blues Revue, "certainly worthy of greater recognition." The release of his first recording for Blind Pig Records, Love Gotcha, should bring him the national and international acclamation he deserves. Jones was born in Seattle into a musical family, which moved to Portland soon afterward. "I remember music was everywhere in our house growing up. My dad was playing Dixieland jazz records and trying to teach me to play trumpet when I was only five years old. My older brother played drums and showed me how. Then he took me to his band rehearsals and had me playing gigs when I was just 13. He took me to see James Brown in '64. You've got to imagine James in '64 - ouch! Then B.B. King, Buddy Guy, even Sonny Terry and Brownie McGhee - all this before I was out of high school. I was underage and totally mesmerized" Jones got deep into the blues and was the leader of Portland's most popular blues bands, Brown Sugar, in the early 70's. "We got to work with touring musicians in those days, like Charlie Musselwhite, George "Harmonica" Smith, the Johnny Otis show, Big Mama Thornton and Big Walter Horton. That's how we learned, and that's really when I first picked up the guitar. A lot of times these people would stay at our homes and teach us music and history. Some of them have passed now, so I cherish those memories. S.P. Leary, who was in Muddy Waters band and was playing drums with Big Walter at the time, leaned over to me as he was leaving town and said, "Man, I'm getting old. You gotta keep it alive. It's a struggle sometimes, but if you love it, you keep on struggling."' Through the years Jones would continue to hone his craft by performing with the likes of Albert Collins, Robert Cray, Bonnie Raitt, Taj Mahal, B.B. King, Dr. John, John Hammond, Etta James, Junior Wells and Buddy Guy, and many more music legends. In the 80's Jones joined forces with ex-Robert Cray singer/harp player Curtis Salgado in a band called In Yo' Face. "That was one fun band! Seemed like we all had the same record collection. Curtis really pushed me as a guitar player, and when he left in '85 to join Roomful of Blues I knew it was time to play my music." Jones knew what he wanted to say and how he wanted to say it. The Lloyd Jones Struggle started in 1985 as a vehicle for his songwriting. "I love a good story. Most of the traditional blues stayed with a shuffle or slow blues. Being a drummer I keep hearing the rhythm of the words all broke down funky and swamp-afied; nice and relaxed but kind of turned inside out." Jones made two recordings in the late 80's for Criminal Records: The Lloyd Jones Struggle \(1987\) and Small Potatoes \(1989\). They won over a dozen local music awards, as well as acclaim from national music publications such as Down Beat and Guitar Player, which in turn led to some extensive touring for the band on the Miller Beer Sponsorship Program. In 1993 Jones released his third album, Lloyd \`Have Mercy' Jones - Live! on the Burnside Records label. In 1995 Lloyd Jones recorded a highly acclaimed album for the Audio Quest label, entitled Trouble Monkey. Blues Revue named it, "not only one of the best albums of 1995, it is one of the best albums of the 1990's," while Robert Cray called it "the best damn record I've heard in a long time!" Vintage Guitar Magazine said, "Jones offers vocals that would make Sam and Dave smile and guitar work Steve Cropper would be proud of" and referred to his affecting vocals as "gritty as a dirt road and smooth as melting butter." Lloyd's songwriting was starting to be noticed as well, with Joe Louis Walker and Gatemouth Brown covering two of his compositions. Jones and his band have become a mainstay on the West Coast circuit, and have brought their tasteful, crowd-pleasing brand of music from New Orleans to Canada to the Caribbean, where Delbert McClinton witnessed a performance and remarked, "When I heard Lloyd Jones live for the first time in January 1999, it was like exhaling after holding my breath for fifteen years." It was such a typically memorable set at the Santa Cruz Blues Festival that led to Jones' signing by Blind Pig Records. Jones describes his soulful and intelligent fusion of funk, blues, and R&B as "storytelling with a Memphis groove." His latest CD, Love Gotcha, presents Lloyd's writing at its trenchant best. His songs have the quality that makes them sound as if they have been around as blues standards for years or they seem to have fallen out of some time warp from the golden days of R&B. His approach to the guitar is both economical and rhythmically sophisticated, with a style that can be as delicate as it is devastating. And Jones' accomplished guitar and vocal work are complemented throughout the recording by some of the funkiest horn-rhythm-organ arrangements around. Blues lovers everywhere are about to discover what Lloyd Jones' fans already know - one taste of his beguiling music and you're captivated. Lloyd's gotcha! Blind Pig Records A division of Whole Hog, Inc. PO. Box 2344, San Francisco, CA 94126

events.summary: Curated by Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK School and Lisa Jarrett Drawing from the Museum’s collection, this exhibition is co-curated by Lisa Jarrett, an artist, educator, and curator, and the Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK Elementary— a group of 4th and 5th grade curators from KSMoCA. Working from a conversation with notable curators Dr. Lowery Stokes Sims and Dr. Leslie King Hammond, the exhibition engages PAM’s collection in new dialogues shaped by emerging curatorial voices and multigenerational knowledge. From theme and concept development, through work selection, and installation, this community curators project highlights the collaborative nature of curatorial practice and museum work. Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK School \(HTC\) is a KSMoCA project. Students participate directly in shaping exhibitions, positioning them as contributors to the museum, and engaging them as researchers, writers, planners, and curators. Through workshops and field trips, students collaborate with artists, visiting curators, and mentors from Portland State University’s College of the Arts. They research how exhibitions are developed, how artworks are interpreted, and how institutional decisions shape public understanding. Expanded curatorial practice includes visual art, writing, performance, research, publishing, and social practice. Co-founded by Lisa Jarrett and Harrell Fletcher, the project began in 2018 at Harriet Tubman Middle School and continues in its current iteration at Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Elementary School.

events.summary: Inspired by Katherine Ace’s 9 Portraits as the foundational starting point for the exhibition, Nine Women Artists will feature the work of the artists shown in Ace’s portrait painting. All mature artists in their careers and with a significant presence in the Northwest, their work reveals a diverse expression of artistic styles from representation to abstraction. There are rich details in the painting. Most notably on the left hangs Henri Fantin-Latour’s A Studio at Les Batignolles, 1870 \(Musée d’Orsay\). In this painting is a formal gathering of male artists. In response to this painting, Katherine asked her subjects to dress in their studio/work clothes as counterpoint, all marked in their characteristic poses. Other Portland women artists are recognized here through their paintings—a small Sally Haley still life hangs in the background, as well as an Amanda Snyder painting behind Phyllis Yes. And to the far right, we have a glimpse of Lucinda Parker’s very large work. Postcards and newspapers scattered on the floor are the exhibition announcements and reviews highlighting the artists’ works. An epic portrait featuring nine women artists of the Northwest, Ace responded to the lack of self-portraits by women artists in history. From left, the artists are: Laura Ross-Paul, Katherine’s self-portrait seated with phone, Mary Josephson, Judy Cooke, Phyllis Yes, Sharon Bronzan, Shu-Ju Wang, Lucinda Parker, and Sherrie Wolf. All are women artists who have made long careers in Portland. As Ace notes about these women, “They have tenacity, have lived through sexist decades, told they couldn’t really be artists—only fit for sleeping with the professor, expected to subvert themselves to male artist machismo.”
events.title: Nine Women Artists

events.summary: Artifact Artist in Residence 10th Annual Holiday Market Where: Showroom of Artifact Creative Recycle 3630 SE Division St Dates: 11/3 thru January 2026 \# of Vendors: 40 Theme: Vivienne Westwood Narnia Forty makers. One showroom. A whole lot of holiday magic. Think 70s Vivienne Westwood meets Narnia: a little rebellious, a little enchanted, and wonderfully weird. Wander through a wonderland of locally made treasures, from ceramics, candles, textiles, and glass art to beanies, body care, bolo ties, sunCATchers, card games, journals, apparel, kitchen must-haves, and all kinds of artful things for your home and everyone on your list. Come curious, shop small, and find something delightfully unexpected. Meet Your Maker Holiday Market Kick Off Party: Friday November 6th 2026 from 6 to 8pm (in conjunction with Division’s 1st Friday) Join us Friday, November 6, from 6 to 8pm for an after-hours shopping party at Artifact! Get first dibs on our Artist in Residence makers and their one-of-a-kind goods at Artifact’s Holiday Market. Makers will be mingling with shoppers, and everyone is invited! Live music from accordion player Robb Obbink and his fiddle partner from Too Loose Cajun Zydeco Band Warm winter drinks from the Riot Bloom Coffee cart Complimentary gift wrapping for your local-maker finds (donations welcome to support Project Lemonade) Raffle kick off and shopping wish lists passed out for Project Lemonade Live portrait drawings by Victoria Herstedt, the perfect personal touch for your holiday cards Community Giveback: Give a Little, Make a Difference, November 4 – December 15 We’re spreading a little holiday magic with a raffle benefiting Project Lemonade! One lucky winner will take home a gift basket featuring an item from each of our Holiday Market Artists in Residence vendors, plus an Artifact gift card. Raffle tickets are $5 each, and 100% of raffle proceeds will benefit Project Lemonade, supporting foster youth across Oregon. Want to give a little more? Artifact will also serve as a drop-off point for Project Lemonade donations from November 4 through December 15. Many of our staff have volunteered with Project Lemonade and have seen firsthand what foster youth need. Together, we’ve put together a wish list of items to help make the season a little brighter: Stuffed animals Books Makeup kits Jewelry Hair accessories Gloves, warm hats, and scarves Packaged socks and underwear Whether you enter the raffle, donate an item, or both, every little bit helps. Let’s make the holidays a little brighter for the kids who need it most.​

events.summary: From Warner Bros. Pictures and Legendary Pictures comes Dune: Part Three, bringing Academy Award-nominated filmmaker Denis Villeneuve’s epic trilogy to a breathtaking conclusion. Dune: Part Three is set nearly two decades after Paul Atreides seized control of the Imperium. Now a ruthless Emperor, Paul must face the consequences of his reign as old allies return, terrifying new threats emerge, and betrayal lurks in every shadow. Haunted by visions of Imperial collapse and the reappearance of his long-lost love, Paul is drawn into a sweeping conspiracy, with Chani at the heart of its unfolding mystery. As rebellion brews and enemies close in, Paul must confront the true cost of power and the fate of those he loves the most. The film stars Oscar nominee Timothée Chalamet, Zendaya, Jason Momoa, Oscar nominee Florence Pugh, Rebecca Ferguson, Isaach de Bankolé, with Oscar nominee Charlotte Rampling, with Anya Taylor-Joy, and Robert Pattinson, and Oscar winner Javier Bardem. Villeneuve directs from a screenplay by Villeneuve and Brian K. Vaughan, based on the novels written by Frank Herbert. The film is produced by Oscar nominees Mary Parent, Cale Boyter, Villeneuve and Tanya Lapointe, and Joe Caracciolo, and executive produced by Joshua Grode, Thomas Tull, Herbert W. Gains, Brian Herbert, Byron Merritt, Kim Herbert, Kevin J. Anderson, Richard P. Rubinstein, John Harrison and Jessica Derhammer. Joining Villeneuve behind the camera are Oscar-winning director of photography Linus Sandgren, Oscar-winning production designer Patrice Vermette, Oscar-winning editor Joe Walker, Oscar nominated costume designer Jacqueline West, Oscar-nominated casting director Francine Maisler, and Oscar-winning composer Hans Zimmer. Warner Bros. Pictures and Legendary Pictures Present A Legendary Pictures Production, A Film By Denis Villeneuve, Dune: Part Three, only in cinemas December 17, 2026. The film will be distributed worldwide by Warner Bros. Pictures and in China by Legendary East.

events.summary: Benson Hotel Annual Gingerbread Display Downtown Editor's Pick Dec. 2, 2025-Jan. 2, 2026 Days vary Free The Benson Portland, Curio Collection by Hilton 309 SW Broadway Portland, OR 97205 Website The following description was submitted by the event organizer. The Benson Portland, Curio Collection by Hilton, invites the community to celebrate one of Portland's most beloved holiday traditions - the 54th Annual Gingerbread Unveiling - filling the hotel's grand lobby with the warmth, wonder, and joy of the season. Guests of all ages are welcome to enjoy live music, children's activities, a hot chocolate station, a surprise visit from Santa, and more as The Benson kicks off the holidays in true Portland style. This year's gingerbread masterpiece remains a closely guarded secret - but whispers from the kitchen hint at a design that may transport visitors to a land of heart, courage, and a touch of magic. As always, the creation promises to be nothing short of spectacular. Leading the culinary artistry once again is Executive Chef David Diffendorfer, who has delighted guests for more than two decades with his intricate, larger-than-life gingerbread displays. Each year, Chef Diffendorfer and his team bring to life imaginative creations that capture the spirit of the season and showcase extraordinary craftsmanship. The Benson is proud to continue its partnership with FOX 12 and Les Schwab Tire Centers' Toy Drive. Guests are encouraged to bring a new, unwrapped toy to help brighten the holidays for local children and families in need. "The Gingerbread Unveiling has been a cherished tradition at The Benson for over five decades," said Ryan Kunzer, General Manager. "Each year, Chef Diffendorfer and his team create something magical that brings the community together in the spirit of the season." The Gingerbread display will remain on view in The Benson's historic lobby throughout the holiday season, inviting guests and visitors alike to experience the wonder of one of Portland's most iconic holiday traditions. Unveiling Festivities begin at 5 p.m., with the unveiling at 6 p.m. on December 2 Saturday, Dec. 13 Sunday, Dec. 14 Monday, Dec. 15 Tuesday, Dec. 16 Wednesday, Dec. 17 Thursday, Dec. 18 Friday, Dec. 19 Saturday, Dec. 20 Sunday, Dec. 21 Monday, Dec. 22 Tuesday, Dec. 23 Wednesday, Dec. 24 Thursday, Dec. 25 Friday, Dec. 26 Saturday, Dec. 27 Sunday, Dec. 28 …and more dates through Jan. 2nd, 2026 More Dates & Times The Benson Portland, Curio Collection by Hilton \(503\) 228-2000 pwelz@bensonhotel.com Art & Design , Exhibitions , Food & Drink , Winter Holidays
