events.summary: Vogue-published photographer Kenji Shimizu, Grammy-nominated producer and artist rei mastrogiovanni, and doctoral candidate in Japanese literature Teppei Fukuda together crafted this selection of photographs that portray Oregon’s four seasons through a critical reimagining of Japanese seasonal aesthetics. Drawing on the visual techniques of sumi-e ink painting, the five sets of photographs express seasonality through portraiture, gesture, everyday objects, and atmosphere. At the same time, the artists are exploring the relationship between tradition and cultural identity as Japanese and multi-heritage Japanese artists living in Oregon, superimposing one of the most prevalent motifs in Japanese art onto a new context. The individual artists’ works will also be on display, as well as artwork from the museum’s collection.

events.summary: Lookout Landscape is an immersive art exhibition by Oregon-based artist and designer David Buckley Borden and a team of collaborators working across forestry, design, and engineering. Inspired by fire lookout towers, trail culture, and backcountry gear, the exhibition invites visitors onto a fabricated “Lookout Trail,” where a series of imaginative scenes—from a trailhead to a weather station, campground, and tool shed—reimagine the visual language of forestry and outdoor culture in the Pacific Northwest. Blending research, humor, and design, the exhibition explores the complex relationships between people and working forests, with wildfire as an underlying thread. As visitors move through the space, they are encouraged to reflect on how forests are shaped, valued, and cared for, and to consider their own connection to these landscapes. Plan your visit and explore the exhibition: worldforestry.org/lookout-landscape
events.title: Lookout Landscape Exhibition

events.summary: This former Southern Pacific Railroad station, fondly called the Old Train Station \(OTS\), is home to Friends of Historic Forest Grove. The Old Train Station now serves as a museum highlighting about 150 years of local history, from photographs and maps to clothing and furniture. It also houses an historic library and research center. Built in 1913, the station handled passenger and light freight service into 1929. After that only light freight came through. Burlingham and Sons purchased the building as office space for their seed company. Unfortunately, over the years this building has gone through some internal and external changes but some of the original station remains and can easy be found. Woodfold acquired the building from Burlingham and has graciously allowed Friends to use the building since 2008. Please stop by and see what we have to offer. Check website to confirm open hours
events.title: Friends of Historic Forest Grove Museum & Library Open

events.summary: Curated by Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK School and Lisa Jarrett Drawing from the Museum’s collection, this exhibition is co-curated by Lisa Jarrett, an artist, educator, and curator, and the Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK Elementary— a group of 4th and 5th grade curators from KSMoCA. Working from a conversation with notable curators Dr. Lowery Stokes Sims and Dr. Leslie King Hammond, the exhibition engages PAM’s collection in new dialogues shaped by emerging curatorial voices and multigenerational knowledge. From theme and concept development, through work selection, and installation, this community curators project highlights the collaborative nature of curatorial practice and museum work. Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK School \(HTC\) is a KSMoCA project. Students participate directly in shaping exhibitions, positioning them as contributors to the museum, and engaging them as researchers, writers, planners, and curators. Through workshops and field trips, students collaborate with artists, visiting curators, and mentors from Portland State University’s College of the Arts. They research how exhibitions are developed, how artworks are interpreted, and how institutional decisions shape public understanding. Expanded curatorial practice includes visual art, writing, performance, research, publishing, and social practice. Co-founded by Lisa Jarrett and Harrell Fletcher, the project began in 2018 at Harriet Tubman Middle School and continues in its current iteration at Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Elementary School.
events.title: Harriet Tubman Center Museum

events.summary: Inspired by Katherine Ace’s 9 Portraits as the foundational starting point for the exhibition, Nine Women Artists will feature the work of the artists shown in Ace’s portrait painting. All mature artists in their careers and with a significant presence in the Northwest, their work reveals a diverse expression of artistic styles from representation to abstraction. There are rich details in the painting. Most notably on the left hangs Henri Fantin-Latour’s A Studio at Les Batignolles, 1870 \(Musée d’Orsay\). In this painting is a formal gathering of male artists. In response to this painting, Katherine asked her subjects to dress in their studio/work clothes as counterpoint, all marked in their characteristic poses. Other Portland women artists are recognized here through their paintings—a small Sally Haley still life hangs in the background, as well as an Amanda Snyder painting behind Phyllis Yes. And to the far right, we have a glimpse of Lucinda Parker’s very large work. Postcards and newspapers scattered on the floor are the exhibition announcements and reviews highlighting the artists’ works. An epic portrait featuring nine women artists of the Northwest, Ace responded to the lack of self-portraits by women artists in history. From left, the artists are: Laura Ross-Paul, Katherine’s self-portrait seated with phone, Mary Josephson, Judy Cooke, Phyllis Yes, Sharon Bronzan, Shu-Ju Wang, Lucinda Parker, and Sherrie Wolf. All are women artists who have made long careers in Portland. As Ace notes about these women, “They have tenacity, have lived through sexist decades, told they couldn’t really be artists—only fit for sleeping with the professor, expected to subvert themselves to male artist machismo.”
events.title: Nine Women Artists

events.summary: Decades after her first fabled Nutcracker fever dream, Clara, no longer the child she once was, finds herself once again tumbling into a world of wonderment. Step into a holiday where tradition is turned upside down and inside out. ’Twas the Night Before Nutcracker is a glittering, whimsical journey through Clara’s holiday eve. What begins with a lively soirée and an innocent absinthe toast unravels into a dreamscape of marching soldiers, mischievous mice, swirling snowflakes, and sugarplum visions. Set to Can Can’s original adaptation of the iconic Nutcracker score, the show features new original songs alongside beloved holiday classics, a festive script, magical choreography, and stunning visuals. The spectacle weaves together classic, modern, aerial, and burlesque performances with Can Can’s refined cabaret style. Sprinkle in the perfect amount of comedy, and a touch of theatrical spark, and you’ve got a show as enchanting as it is unexpected. With its blend of elegance, humor, high kicks, and holiday spirit, ‘Twas the Night Before Nutcracker is a new holiday tradition in the making.

Known for their eclectic sound that seamlessly blends blues, funk, psychedelic rock, and jazz, the band has established a vibrant presence in the local New York and New Orleans music scene. Drawing from legends like The Doors, Marcus King, Chris Cain, and more, the band blends their roots to craft an experience that's as gritty as New York, as soulful as New Orleans, and as laid-back as Oregon. Fronted by brothers Jesse Jake & Cody Luke, the band rips through powerful vocals, fiery guitar solos, and an unstoppable stage presence. Their horn section hits hard with bold, brass-driven grooves that amp up every track. Known for their original music, Kota Dosa mixes their own songs with their favorite influences from across genres. Whether tearing up big stages or bringing their creative energy to rainy streets and front porches, they own every crowd, proving their versatility in any setting. events.summary: JERRY JOSEPH & THE JACKMORMONS with LordymamaDoors: 7:00pm Show: 8:00pm Ages: 21+ Jerry Joseph is a musician who lives in Portland Oregon, but he's often gone. He's been inducted into the Oregon Music Hall of Fame but is still rather obscure to a lot of people. He plays well over 150 shows a year in the usual places. Across America. Sometimes in Europe, Mexico, and Central America. Then there's these other places he plays---Lebanon, Israel, Kurdish Iraq, India, and Afghanistan. All over the Middle East, often in war zones and refugee camps. Jerry, to me is a cult figure who could, in some alternate reality, have easily been one of the biggest stars in the world. One of the greatest live performers I have ever seen and long one of my favorite songwriters. I can't hear the chorus of San Acacia without picturing Jerry singing it in front of 100,000 screaming fans, in a soccer stadium in Brazil. In the pouring rain. With everyone singing along. Exerped from Essay by Patterson Hood

events.summary: The Mike Dillon Band, featuring Brad Haas & Otto SchrangSoul'd Out Presents: An Evening with The Mike Dillon Band, featuring Brad Haas & Otto Schrang: Mike & Beignet Go To The Zoo From the ever prolific mind of Mike Dillon comes Mike & Beignet Go to the Zoo, an 11-track, multi-dimensional percussion and vibraphone album. What began as an exploration of loss, would transform into a celebration of life, friendship, and the enduring spirit of a 5.6-pound Papillon named Beignet, the tiny pup who became Dillon's constant tour companion, by his side for thousands of miles. The compositions were born from the grief of losing friends and influences. In a pivot to find light in the dark, Dillon decided to metaphorically transform those humans into animals, reimagining the LP as a joyful trip to the zoo with his dog. Highlights include the ghostly yet elegant , "rdquo" -> Honey The Peregrine," a stately tribute to the late Ellis Marsalis entitled , "rdquo" -> Ellis the Penguin," and , "rdquo" -> Puma & The Spider Monkey," an analog synth Cumbia. It winds through psychedelia like , "rdquo" -> Gorilla & Zebra Birthday Party," the electro-jungle boogie-funk of , "rdquo" -> Gibby Plays Possum" and closes with the mournful elegy , "rdquo" -> Beignet Greets the Owl." Mike Dillon is a longtime collaborator of artists like Les Claypool and Rickie Lee Jones. This latest effort completes a loose trilogy of solo instrumental releases following Functioning Broke (2016) and Rosewood (2020). events.summary:
Code & Coffee is an inclusive, informal co-working session: drink your beverage of choice, bring your laptop, and hang out with your peers! Have engaging conversations, or focus on work or projects. This is a great opportunity to learn from others, share your knowledge, and possibly collaborate on side projects, online courses, or even your day-to-day work.

---- Schedule ----

You're welcome to drop in anytime during the event. We understand that everyone may have external commitments and challenges - join us when you can!

We have informal unscheduled introductions - practice your personal elevator pitch, or take things slower to build your confidence.

---- Venue ----

Peet's Coffee allow us to informally and freely use their space. If within your budget, we'd appreciate your help to sustain our use of the venue, by purchasing something tasty, whether Chai or otherwise.

Find us at tables with a Code&Coffee sign - or a clump of laptop-users!

Wifi and power outlets are available.

Our meeting area should be accessible - please let us know if not.

---- What to expect ----

Smaller events than you may be used to, with a mixed crowd week-to-week. We expect this is likely due to us meeting weekly, at a less central location.

These may result in what you're looking for:

A smaller, less intimidating, lower pressure, cozy atmosphere.

A mix of regular and new faces.

A simpler schedule - every week, same time, same place - that you can drop into when you like.

Being closer to you than other events.

Whether those are generally or partly to your liking, we hope you'll consider dropping by sometime!

---- Getting to the venue ----

Look for the venue on the meetup Google map, or alternatives like OpenStreetMap.

-- Driving --

There are limited parking spaces on a lot outside the venue (4+1 accessible), with more in the surrounding area.

-- Transit options --

Beaverton Central (Red/Blue MAX), then walk~ 8 minutes

Beaverton Transit Center (Red/Blue MAX, bus, WES) then walk ~11 minutes

For a shorter walk to the venue, take a bus from Beaverton Transit Center (52 to Farmington/Hall, 76 to Watson/Broadway, 57 to Canyon/Watson)

---- Supporting the events ----

Purchasing items from the venue helps us maintain a healthy relationship with them.

In addition, if you attend semi-regularly then please consider becoming a co-host. This reduces the load on other co-hosts, and provides backup for the event if another is unable to attend. To get involved, please chat with a co-host at an event!

--- Links ---

Still uncertain?

Information on the wider Portland Code & Coffee group is available on meetup. The channel #portland-general is available for the group to chat on Discord.

That and the set of nationwide Discord channels may be accessed at codeandcoffee.chat, or the Discord button at codeandcoffee.org.

Further information about the central Code&Coffee organization and their other events is available on their website.

events.summary: Jack London Revue Presents Grandifolia Doors: 7:00pm Show: 8:00pm 21+ Grandifolia is an alternative rock band born out of the Pacific Northwest music scene. The project began in Portland, Oregon in 2017 when guitarist Harold Forsyth approached drummer Chris Gutendorf with a collection of powerful, unreleased tunes. Recognizing the potential of the music, the duo immediately set out to form a band. The lineup came together quickly and naturally. Guitarist Rob Murphey joined shortly after, followed by Chris's close friend, Kerry Montgomery, who took over the bass. To complete their sound, Chris reached out to Isaiah Brown---a childhood friend from growing up near Mt. Hood---to step up to the microphone. Isaiah joined immediately, bringing the compelling vocal presence the band needed. The band quickly channeled this chemistry into the studio, releasing their debut EP, Blouse. Building on that momentum, they followed up with their first full-length album, Yesterday's Cul De Sac, which the first song on the album was featured in Climate Pledge Arena at a Seattle Kraken game this past October in 2026. Driven by authentic songwriting and deep-rooted chemistry, Grandifolia continues to carve out their own space in the modern rock landscape, as they are set to release a new album in 2027. This upcoming show at the Jack London Revue will be special for the fans to hear some of the new songs live before the album gets released! events.summary: Kimaya Diggs with Lexie, Les AilesSoul'd Out Presents: Kimaya Diggs with special guests Lexie, Les Ailes Doors: 7:00pm Show: 8:00pm Ages 21+. https://www.kimayadiggs.com/ When Kimaya Diggs thinks of green, she thinks first of her backyard in summer. Her house sits against woods that open onto a farm, and in the warm months the whole place seems to layer itself: trees over trees, native plants, birds, insects, and the deep living texture of land that has been tended carefully. When she moved there, the landscape was crowded with invasive plants. For years, she has worked to bring it back into balance. That image became the beginning of Green, her new album out October 2nd: a record about growth that has been happening quietly for a long time, then arrives all at once. , "rdquo" -> To me, green captures the seasonal moment when the first leaves come out," Diggs says. , "rdquo" -> There's no other moment where the landscape transforms so rapidly. The transition from summer into fall is very slow, but the transition from winter into just that moment of all the leaves coming out is so extraordinary to me. And it feels like some of the personal growth that I've made, which feels like it's taken a long time to come and then, when it comes, it comes suddenly." For Diggs, a musician, songwriter, poet, producer, and world-builder from Western Massachusetts, Green marks a moment of arrival. Newly off supporting dates with Mavis Staples, Emily King, Trombone Shorty, and Tank & the Bangas, she enters this album with a clearer sense of her own authority: as a vocalist, as a storyteller, and, for the first time in such a complete way, as the lead producer directing the shape of the record. Don't miss Kimaya's debut at the Jack London Revue on January 18, 2027! -------------------------------- Notes on Seating: Open seating, may be limited or standing room only. events.summary: Early Show - Black Tie/White NoiseDoors: 6:00pm Show: 7:00pm Ages 21+ oin us for the seventh installment of Black Tie/White Noise, where The Christopher Brown Quartet will perform David Bowie's 1977 album, Low, in its entirety. The first LP of the famous Berlin Trilogy, Low is regarded as the Rosetta Stone to the post-punk and post-rock lineage. In regards to the emotional approach of sonic atmosphere and most significantly, the production, there is no doubt to the confidence of David Bowie's indulgence in his , "rdquo" -> sound and vision" and his bravery to be an artist at all costs (so much so that RCA tried to hinder the album's release.) It's with this in mind that The Christopher Brown Quartet evaluates, dissects and reassembles the songs from this seminal record. Be prepared! John Nastos (Alto Sax & EWI) Chris Clark-Johnson (Electric Guitar) Greg Goebel (Keyboards) Damian Erskine (Electric Bass) Christopher Brown (Drums) For more information on Days of Bowie, including other events, please visit daysofbowie.com While the Christopher Brown Quartet has been active since 2014, it has arguably been the busiest jazz group in Portland since 2017. And just like his father [Mel Brown] before him, Christopher has been on a quest to further infuse the Portland jazz scene with as many of the same musical and cultural sensibilities as is to be found within the NYC jazz scene. However, what separates this group from many others (in and outside of Portland), is the degree to which their sensibilities are entrenched within the NYC sound of the 1990's, which was marked by a youthful exuberance towards being steeped in as much of the history of music as possible, so as to use those same insights to agitate the boundaries of conventional thought. So given that David Bowie's approach to music follows the same ethos, is why it's so fitting to have the Christopher Brown Quartet navigate his music, so as to further push against the edges of what people would normally expect from Bowie himself. events.summary:
Code & Coffee is an inclusive, informal co-working session: drink your beverage of choice, bring your laptop, and hang out with your peers! Have engaging conversations, or focus on work or projects. This is a great opportunity to learn from others, share your knowledge, and possibly collaborate on side projects, online courses, or even your day-to-day work.

---- Schedule ----

You're welcome to drop in anytime during the event. We understand that everyone may have external commitments and challenges - join us when you can!

We have informal unscheduled introductions - practice your personal elevator pitch, or take things slower to build your confidence.

---- Venue ----

Peet's Coffee allow us to informally and freely use their space. If within your budget, we'd appreciate your help to sustain our use of the venue, by purchasing something tasty, whether Chai or otherwise.

Find us at tables with a Code&Coffee sign - or a clump of laptop-users!

Wifi and power outlets are available.

Our meeting area should be accessible - please let us know if not.

---- What to expect ----

Smaller events than you may be used to, with a mixed crowd week-to-week. We expect this is likely due to us meeting weekly, at a less central location.

These may result in what you're looking for:

A smaller, less intimidating, lower pressure, cozy atmosphere.

A mix of regular and new faces.

A simpler schedule - every week, same time, same place - that you can drop into when you like.

Being closer to you than other events.

Whether those are generally or partly to your liking, we hope you'll consider dropping by sometime!

---- Getting to the venue ----

Look for the venue on the meetup Google map, or alternatives like OpenStreetMap.

-- Driving --

There are limited parking spaces on a lot outside the venue (4+1 accessible), with more in the surrounding area.

-- Transit options --

Beaverton Central (Red/Blue MAX), then walk~ 8 minutes

Beaverton Transit Center (Red/Blue MAX, bus, WES) then walk ~11 minutes

For a shorter walk to the venue, take a bus from Beaverton Transit Center (52 to Farmington/Hall, 76 to Watson/Broadway, 57 to Canyon/Watson)

---- Supporting the events ----

Purchasing items from the venue helps us maintain a healthy relationship with them.

In addition, if you attend semi-regularly then please consider becoming a co-host. This reduces the load on other co-hosts, and provides backup for the event if another is unable to attend. To get involved, please chat with a co-host at an event!

--- Links ---

Still uncertain?

Information on the wider Portland Code & Coffee group is available on meetup. The channel #portland-general is available for the group to chat on Discord.

That and the set of nationwide Discord channels may be accessed at codeandcoffee.chat, or the Discord button at codeandcoffee.org.

Further information about the central Code&Coffee organization and their other events is available on their website.
events.title: PDX Code & Coffee - Happy Valley @ Peet's Coffee

events.summary: An Evening with Trio SubtonicSoul'd Out Presents: An Evening with Trio Subtonic Doors: 7:00PM Show: 8:00PM Ages 21+ Micah Hummel - drums Bill Athens - bass Galen Clark - keys Trio Subtonic is a genre bending power trio out of Portland, Oregon that blends groove heavy funk, experimental soundscapes and soaring soul jazz. Led by keyboardist Galen Clark (Anna Tivel, Outer Orbit, Sleater-Kinney), Subtonic explores a dynamic range of original compositions and reimagined covers, with an emphasis on improvisation and pushing genre boundaries. The band features Micah Hummel (Anna Tivel, Quickly Quickly) on drums and Bill Athens (Sleater-Kinney, Three Leg Torso) on bass. Portland-based genre bending jazz group Trio Subtonic releases their 7th full-length album and first vinyl print, The Space Around You, on December 8, 2026. This is the group's first studio release in nearly ten years. On this album, the trio explores a more experimental and introspective side while retaining the groove heavy sound and dynamic arrangements that distinguish their earlier discography. Imagined as a collection of soundscape stories spanning the last decade, these songs evoke existential disquiet and the moodiness of attachment in a time of change. The Space Around You is an uncompromising exploration of weird sounds, infectious grooves, and the playful interaction of the trio instrumentation. Featured artists include West Coast VIPs such as LA's Nicole McCabe (alto sax), Seattle's Andy Coe (guitar) and Portland's Cyrus Nabipoor (trumpet). ------ JLR Seating Map Notes: For this show, you may reserve individual tables on the map pictured. events.summary: José James Sings Sinatra The celebrated jazz vocalist explores the legacy of one of the greatest American voices of all time. For internationally renowned jazz singer José James, this project is fate. In 2016, James was called by Universal Pictures to perform Sinatra's version of "I've Got You Under My Skin" for the blockbuster film 50 Shades Darker. James---a devoted student of Sinatra---accepted the role and soon found himself in the hallowed halls of Capitol's Studio B, behind the very microphone Sinatra used to record his most celebrated catalog for Capitol Records. "It was a huge honor and a surprise," remembers James. "There was a moment where engineer Al Schmitt brought out the famous Neumann U47, including the wooden box it lives in. On that box, written in black Sharpie in all caps, was just one word---FRANK. Sinatra was letting everyone know that this was his house and anyone who dared to scale the heights of his mountaintop had better be prepared." James rose to the challenge, performing that song onscreen in the film and recording another Sinatra classic, "They Can't Take That Away From Me," for the official movie soundtrack. Following that release, James has been in high demand, performing at the Hollywood Bowl Jazz Festival for both a Frank Sinatra tribute with the Count Basie Orchestra as well as with the Christian McBride Big Band. He also performed with Laura Mvula alongside the Melbourne, Sydney, and Perth Symphony Orchestras, and has been a featured performer with the Jazz at Lincoln Center, Royal Concertgebouw, and Metropole Orchestras. In September 2026, James will release his 14th studio album The Best Is Yet to Come, a groundbreaking reexamination of one of America's greatest voices from the most exciting male jazz singer of the moment. For James, this project is a reclamation---both live and on record---of Sinatra's brilliance as a jazz singer, a rhythmic improviser from the schools of Billie Holiday and Tommy Dorsey. With big band arrangements by the legendary John Clayton, this is no mere nostalgia trip, but a deeper look into the craft and mastery of the Chairman of the Board.
events.title: JOSÉ JAMES SINGS SINATRA

events.summary:
Code & Coffee is an inclusive, informal co-working session: drink your beverage of choice, bring your laptop, and hang out with your peers! Have engaging conversations, or focus on work or projects. This is a great opportunity to learn from others, share your knowledge, and possibly collaborate on side projects, online courses, or even your day-to-day work.

---- Schedule ----

You're welcome to drop in anytime during the event. We understand that everyone may have external commitments and challenges - join us when you can!

We have informal unscheduled introductions - practice your personal elevator pitch, or take things slower to build your confidence.

---- Venue ----

Peet's Coffee allow us to informally and freely use their space. If within your budget, we'd appreciate your help to sustain our use of the venue, by purchasing something tasty, whether Chai or otherwise.

Find us at tables with a Code&Coffee sign - or a clump of laptop-users!

Wifi and power outlets are available.

Our meeting area should be accessible - please let us know if not.

---- What to expect ----

Smaller events than you may be used to, with a mixed crowd week-to-week. We expect this is likely due to us meeting weekly, at a less central location.

These may result in what you're looking for:

A smaller, less intimidating, lower pressure, cozy atmosphere.

A mix of regular and new faces.

A simpler schedule - every week, same time, same place - that you can drop into when you like.

Being closer to you than other events.

Whether those are generally or partly to your liking, we hope you'll consider dropping by sometime!

---- Getting to the venue ----

Look for the venue on the meetup Google map, or alternatives like OpenStreetMap.

-- Driving --

There are limited parking spaces on a lot outside the venue (4+1 accessible), with more in the surrounding area.

-- Transit options --

Beaverton Central (Red/Blue MAX), then walk~ 8 minutes

Beaverton Transit Center (Red/Blue MAX, bus, WES) then walk ~11 minutes

For a shorter walk to the venue, take a bus from Beaverton Transit Center (52 to Farmington/Hall, 76 to Watson/Broadway, 57 to Canyon/Watson)

---- Supporting the events ----

Purchasing items from the venue helps us maintain a healthy relationship with them.

In addition, if you attend semi-regularly then please consider becoming a co-host. This reduces the load on other co-hosts, and provides backup for the event if another is unable to attend. To get involved, please chat with a co-host at an event!

--- Links ---

Still uncertain?

Information on the wider Portland Code & Coffee group is available on meetup. The channel #portland-general is available for the group to chat on Discord.

That and the set of nationwide Discord channels may be accessed at codeandcoffee.chat, or the Discord button at codeandcoffee.org.

Further information about the central Code&Coffee organization and their other events is available on their website.

events.summary: New Orleans-based singer-songwriter Hans Williams makes soulful, dreamy folk shaped by the people and places closest to him. His debut album, Songs for the Neighbors, was born in the backyard o1f his Bayou St. John home, where late-night jams and intimate shows regularly spill over fences and through open windows. Recorded largely live at the house with his longtime band and producer Phin Choukas (Noah Kahan), the record blends folk with touches of soul, funk, psychedelia, and country. At its heart, Songs for the Neighbors is about connection with friends, lovers, family, neighbors, and those no longer here. Warm, intimate, and deeply human, the album captures the feeling of people making music together and Williams belief that even the smallest act of reaching out can bring us closer. Now, Williams is excited to bring Songs for the Neighbors out of the backyard and onto the stage. To play these songs live, see familiar faces, meet new ones, and share the record with the people who have been listening along the way. Hans Williams has partnered with PLUS1 so that $1 per ticket goes to supporting organizations working for equity, access, and dignity for all. www.plus1.org

Trumpeter/saxophonist Marcus Tenney recalls long drives across the state, , "rdquo" -> soaking up the sights, the foliage," experiences that quietly shaped the band's sound. Bassist Andrew Randazzo agrees: , "rdquo" -> All that stuff seeps into the music." Across 15 years, the Richmond quintet, Tenney, Randazzo, Corey Fonville, Morgan Burrs, and DJ Harrison, has merged jazz, hip-hop, soul, funk, and R&B into a lane all their own. Their newest album, Letters from the Atlantic (on Concord Jazz), plays like an East Coast travelogue, from the Chesapeake Bay to New York and down to Florida. Recorded at Spacebomb Studios with Producer Chris Dunn and engineer Alex Dejong, the project leans into house, dance, and jazz influences while highlighting a remarkable cast of guests, including Melanie Charles, Leanor Wolf, Mia Gladstone, Yaya Bey, Victoria Victoria, Nicholas Payton, and Neal Francis. From the serene opener , "rdquo" -> Seagulls" to a celestial take on Wayne Shorter's , "rdquo" -> Infant Eyes," the album captures Butcher Brown's evolving, instinctive artistry honest, unforced, and distinctly their own.

events.summary: Soul'd Out Presents: Horse Lords with Mariam Rezaei Doors: 7:00pm Show: 8:00pm Ages: 21+ https://www.horselords.org/ Horse Lords were founded in Baltimore, Maryland in 2010; they evolved from the experimental collective Teeth Mountain and began as a trio with drummer Sam Haberman, guitarist Owen Gardner, and bassist Max Eilbacher, soon adding alto saxophonist Andrew Bernstein to the core ensemble. Though Horse Lords grew out of the fertile Baltimore noise and leftfield rock scene, a storied environment for artists and weirdos that has nurtured many an influential outsider band (Lungfish, Matmos), their approach is more omnivorous than the stippled rhythms of instrumental electric rock would indicate. Across sixteen years of frequent touring, Horse Lords have released ten studio, live, and collaboration albums in addition to a split EP with fellow Baltimoreans Lower Dens, a handful of singles and compilation tracks. For RVNG's FRKWYS series, the band collaborated with Berlin-based composer Arnold Dreyblatt, a onetime student of La Monte Young and Pauline Oliveros whose just intonation chamber music was a crucial part of the post-Fluxus Downtown New York City environment. For their second studio album on RVNG Intl., Demand To Be Taken To Heaven Alive!, Horse Lords have followed this notion and augmented the instrumentation, expanding the format slightly to include bass clarinetist Madison Greenstone (TAK Ensemble), trombonist Weston Olencki (Nate Wooley, RAGE Thormbones) and vocalists Nina Guo (Departure Duo) and Evelyn Saylor (Holly Herndon, Caterina Barbieri) across a program of twelve original compositions. As the members are keen to point out, Demand To Be Taken To Heaven Alive! is , "rdquo" -> a bid for the flattening of time and perception in favor of greater goods [and] the iterative nature of reaching/building a paradise in this life, not the next," and the new album at hand is an illuminating starting point for eternal nowness.

events.summary: The LiminanasStar Theater Presents: The Liminanas Doors: 8:00pm Show: 9:00pm Ages: 21+ ----- Hailing from a small town in the South of France, Lionel and Marie Limiñana aka The Limiñanas reinvent the 1960s French yéyé heritage by fusing it with modern rock. Their unique style blends the rebellious spirit and aesthetic of the Gainsbourg and Bardot era with contemporary garage and psychedelic sounds. Singing in French & English and collaborating with a diverse array of artists, The Limiñanas have a unique ability to distill the cachet of a nostalgic, highly cinematic era while revisiting it through a modern lens.

events.summary: Watch as world class drivers take Hot Wheels vehicles through a series of stunt challenges, with each competition getting more difficult and even more epic. Witness iconic Hot Wheels cars, Street Bikes, and ATVs execute precision driving skills, backflips, ramp jumps, take on the iconic 45 feet tall 360 loop and more! Featuring interactive fan experiences, larger than life Hot Wheels displays, and special appearances by legendary Hot Wheels vehicles including GT Scorcher, Boneshaker, Rodger Dodger and more. Hot Wheels Stunt Show is the next level experience for fans of all ages. Whether you are a die hard collector or a young challenger dreaming of racing glory, this show is a must see, edge of your seat experience for audiences of all ages.

events.summary:
Code & Coffee is an inclusive, informal co-working session: drink your beverage of choice, bring your laptop, and hang out with your peers! Have engaging conversations, or focus on work or projects. This is a great opportunity to learn from others, share your knowledge, and possibly collaborate on side projects, online courses, or even your day-to-day work.

---- Schedule ----

You're welcome to drop in anytime during the event. We understand that everyone may have external commitments and challenges - join us when you can!

We have informal unscheduled introductions - practice your personal elevator pitch, or take things slower to build your confidence.

---- Venue ----

Peet's Coffee allow us to informally and freely use their space. If within your budget, we'd appreciate your help to sustain our use of the venue, by purchasing something tasty, whether Chai or otherwise.

Find us at tables with a Code&Coffee sign - or a clump of laptop-users!

Wifi and power outlets are available.

Our meeting area should be accessible - please let us know if not.

---- What to expect ----

Smaller events than you may be used to, with a mixed crowd week-to-week. We expect this is likely due to us meeting weekly, at a less central location.

These may result in what you're looking for:

A smaller, less intimidating, lower pressure, cozy atmosphere.

A mix of regular and new faces.

A simpler schedule - every week, same time, same place - that you can drop into when you like.

Being closer to you than other events.

Whether those are generally or partly to your liking, we hope you'll consider dropping by sometime!

---- Getting to the venue ----

Look for the venue on the meetup Google map, or alternatives like OpenStreetMap.

-- Driving --

There are limited parking spaces on a lot outside the venue (4+1 accessible), with more in the surrounding area.

-- Transit options --

Beaverton Central (Red/Blue MAX), then walk~ 8 minutes

Beaverton Transit Center (Red/Blue MAX, bus, WES) then walk ~11 minutes

For a shorter walk to the venue, take a bus from Beaverton Transit Center (52 to Farmington/Hall, 76 to Watson/Broadway, 57 to Canyon/Watson)

---- Supporting the events ----

Purchasing items from the venue helps us maintain a healthy relationship with them.

In addition, if you attend semi-regularly then please consider becoming a co-host. This reduces the load on other co-hosts, and provides backup for the event if another is unable to attend. To get involved, please chat with a co-host at an event!

--- Links ---

Still uncertain?

Information on the wider Portland Code & Coffee group is available on meetup. The channel #portland-general is available for the group to chat on Discord.

That and the set of nationwide Discord channels may be accessed at codeandcoffee.chat, or the Discord button at codeandcoffee.org.

Further information about the central Code&Coffee organization and their other events is available on their website.
